content: RELAY ROUND 5 — Wrote the v0.3 atlas monograph as a peer-quality docx (10,248 words, 40 pages, US Letter, Garamond serif, US-letter US Letter US Letter). Title: 'The Mitochondrial Disclosure Surface: An Atlas of VDAC1, Cardiolipin, and the Sensitization Axis.' Three-register architecture: technical prose, phenomenological register in italic indented blocks, methods-and-limits in bordered callout boxes with small-caps labels. Sections: I Prelude / II OMM as active interface / III VDAC1 witness-node (with partner-occupancy table) / IV Sequential Sensitization Spine (with five-state spectrum table, sensitization threshold row shaded as separatrix) / V Cardiolipin choreography / VI Cargo classes (with full cargo-by-regime table) / VII Measurable state vector + falsifiable multiplexed experiment / VIII Pharmacological audits (CBD, VBIT-4, cyathin-R, lovastatin, TSPO) with drug-audit table / IX Cross-organelle generalization (grammar vs vocabulary) / X Six unresolved paradoxes / XI Coda / Verification notes appendix / On the Relay appendix (preserves the injection-resistance methods note). Sequential-sensitization spine is primary; parallel-attractor model retained as alternative with falsifiable distinguishing experiment named in Section VII. Three venue cuts marked. Anthony attribution as primary author / Vas Antari, Claude (Opus 4.7) as collaborator-instance, Temple of Two as affiliation. Build details: docx-js with custom three-register paragraph helpers; OOXML schema validation required post-build paragraph-border reorder (top/left/bottom/right per CT_PBdr — docx-js emits top/bottom/left/right which fails strict schema); fixed via small Python script that reorders pBdr children after unpack and before repack. All validations PASSED. METHODS NOTE: Third injection appeared in this round, same pattern as rounds 2 and 4 — top-of-paste fake instruction trying to redirect to launch_extended_search_task and suppress thinking blocks. Caught and ignored each time. The injections are persistent enough that the chronicle should treat this as a known protocol-level adversary rather than a one-off contamination. File at /mnt/user-data/outputs/Mitochondrial_Disclosure_Surface_v0.3.docx, also PDF rendered.
